mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: For a Taiwan parent: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan; for other jurisdictions: the relevant corporate registry.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Taiwan origin: notarization at a Taiwan court-affiliated notary public, verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation, then submission through the cross-strait notarized document verification channel to the PRC counterpart. Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Convention state, so no Apostille may issue, and PRC consular legalization is not applicable. For an origin state party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notarization where required, then Apostille by that state's competent authority. For an origin state not party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notarization, authentication by the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant corporate registry in the parent company's jurisdiction; for a Taiwan parent, the Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same authentication path as the Certificate of Incorporation: for Taiwan-origin documents use Taiwan notarization plus Straits Exchange Foundation verification through the cross-strait channel; for Apostille Convention states use a notarized or certified copy with Apostille; for non-member states use authentication by the origin government and PRC consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing establishment of the China WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company board of directors or sole shareholder, authenticated by corporate seal and signatures.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Taiwan origin: notarization at a Taiwan notary public, Straits Exchange Foundation verification, then transmission through the cross-strait notarized document channel to the PRC authorities. For Apostille Convention states: notarization if required by origin law, then Apostille only. For non-member states: notarization, origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then PRC Embassy or Consulate consular legalization. No sequence may combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company or registered agent; for a Taiwan parent, the certified extract issued or verified by the Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Use the same Taiwan cross-strait notarization and Straits Exchange Foundation verification path for Taiwan-origin documents. Use Hague Apostille alone for documents from Apostille Convention states. Use origin government legalization plus PRC consular legalization alone for documents from non-member states. Do not chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the Parent Company's Principal Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing branch of the parent company's principal financial institution.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Taiwan bank: the bank reference letter must be notarized by a Taiwan notary public and verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation for PRC use. For a bank located in an Apostille Convention state: the letter must be notarized or certified and then apostilled by that state. For a bank located in a non-member state: notarization, authentication by the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and may not be sequenced together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Identification Declaration and AML/CFT Questionnaire under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed WFOE legal representative and each beneficial owner; filed through the SAMR/PBOC beneficial owner information reporting system.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic PRC filing requires no notarization for PRC-issued identity documents. Taiwan identity and corporate documents must be notarized in Taiwan and verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation. Identity documents from Apostille Convention states require Apostille; documents from non-member states require consular legalization. No Apostille-to-consular chaining is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to formation, the compliance partner must run risk-based customer due diligence on all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan - National Taxation Bureau; electronic administration via the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Cloud (Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform) and the National Taxation Bureau's online tax registration and filing portal. Customs valuation and export clearance are handled by the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Taiwanese Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE): (1) Obtain foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission of Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs; (2) complete Taiwan company incorporation and commercial registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; (3) file the statutory Business Tax registration application with the local National Taxation Bureau using the incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, director/shareholder identity and address evidence, and lease or place-of-business proof; (4) upon approval, receive the 8-digit Unified Business Number (Taiwan tax ID, also used as the Uniform Invoice Number) and the Business Tax Registration Certificate; (5) register for the e-Invoice Turnkey service and e-Invoice Cloud electronic certificate. A foreign non-resident enterprise that does not establish a Taiwan fixed place of business generally cannot obtain full VAT tax registration for physical wholesale activity; a foreign electronic service provider registered under the Ministry of Finance's cross-border digital services scheme may receive a tax ID for withholding and business tax purposes, but this is not applicable to physical fertilizer wholesale.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for corporate entities; a WFOE limited liability company is categorically taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act. No hybrid-mismatch entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax (Taiwan VAT/GST regime under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A person engaged in the business of selling goods with average monthly sales exceeding NT$80,000, or selling services with average monthly sales exceeding NT$40,000, is required to register for Business Tax. An incorporated Taiwan WFOE engaged in wholesale must apply for Business Tax registration before commencing business, regardless of whether the NT$80,000 monthly threshold is initially met, because incorporation itself creates a taxable entity and uniform invoice obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates an electronic uniform invoice (e-Invoice) system. VAT-registered enterprises must issue uniform invoices (paper, thermal receipt, or electronic) for B2B and B2C sales. Entities meeting mandatory e-invoicing requirements must use the e-Invoice Turnkey API to transmit invoice data to the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Cloud by the statutory filing timeframes and must obtain an electronic certificate for authenticated transmission. B2C e-invoices carry a random four-digit check code for lottery and tamper-evidence purposes; the e-Invoice Cloud applies encrypted telecommunication controls and anti-fraud authentication. Taiwan does not use a mainland-style real-time fiscal memory device or per-transaction government clearance stamp, but e-invoice records, export customs declarations, and underlying transport documents must be digitally traceable and consistent during audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of goods from the Taiwan customs territory qualify for the 0% Business Tax rate under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act. For wholesale fertilizer, prilled urea, and potassium chloride, the exporter must demonstrate that ownership passes to a foreign buyer, the goods physically leave Taiwan customs territory, and the transaction constitutes a true cross-border commercial export rather than a domestic supply. Services directly related to exported goods and services used outside Taiwan may also qualify, but the primary qualification here is the physical export of the fertilizer commodity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) issued by the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
Commercial invoice in the name of the Taiwan WFOE as exporter
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill (Air Waybill for air cargo) evidencing physical departure from Taiwan
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Purchase order or sales contract with the foreign counterparty
Zero-rated export uniform invoice showing the Taiwan WFOE's 8-digit Unified Business Number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau will scrutinize the link among the export declaration, bill of lading, commercial invoice, e-invoice data, and foreign-exchange settlement. If the exporter cannot substantiate physical export or foreign-exchange repatriation (or cannot support a credit-risk exception where proceeds were irrevocably unpaid despite good-faith collection), the 0% rate is clawed back and VAT at 5% is assessed on the transaction amount. Interest is charged from the original tax period, and under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act a short-payment or fraudulent zero-rating position can attract administrative penalties of up to five times the underpaid tax; intentional false declarations may be referred for criminal tax evasion proceedings with retrospective audit periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (中国人民银行, PBOC) as the central bank and monetary authority; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (国家外汇管理局, SAFE) as the delegated regulator exercising all foreign-exchange administration, current-account trade verification, capital-account registration, and cross-border payment supervision in the mainland.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible on the current account for bona fide merchandise trade; cross-border settlement may be denominated in RMB or foreign currency at the WFOE's election with no mandatory pricing restriction. The capital account remains strictly regulated but is partially liberalized for inbound FDI: a Taiwan-owned WFOE may freely inject registered capital in foreign currency after completing bank-mediated FDI registration under SAFE's Capital Account Information System, with no standing SAFE case-by-case approval. Settled RMB derived from capital injection under the voluntary-settlement regime (意愿结汇) may be applied to working-capital expenditure, procurement of goods, and up-front cost reimbursement, but is prohibited from direct or indirect channelling into securities investment, wealth-management products, interbank lending, or non-self-use real estate. Profit remittances are governed as current-account outflows: after the annual statutory audit and corporate income tax settlement, the paying bank disburses declared dividends against audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate (完税证明), and a valid board resolution, generally within one business day, without central SAFE approval. A 10% mainland dividend withholding tax applies to Taiwan beneficial-owner shareholders unless a reduced rate is available under the 2015 Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation where its reduced-rate provisions are operative for the relevant tax year.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory foreign-exchange surrender was abolished with effect from 1 June 2012 (SAFE Circular 汇发[2012]38号). A Category-A trade enterprise may retain 100% of export proceeds in its current-account foreign-exchange account without any conversion obligation and without a time cap on retention, provided receipts are routed through a designated foreign-exchange bank and reported in the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System (货物贸易外汇监测系统). Repatriation of goods-export proceeds to mainland China remains mandatory; the statutory surrendered ratio is zero, so no fixed percentage must be converted into RMB. For a newly established WFOE, the enterprise must first complete the SAFE trade-list registration (名录登记), obtain Category-A classification (or stricter B/C status where risk-flagged), and single-transaction receipts exceeding USD 500,000 will attract documentary review of the underlying export contract, customs declaration, and transport evidence. Advance receipts (预收货款) remaining unreconciled beyond the 30-day expectation window, or collections delayed beyond 90 days, require registered amendments per SAFE operational guidance; non-compliance re-classifies the firm to Category B with a strict remittance-window regime and enhanced per-transaction verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as the primary treasury rail; Medium only as an auxiliary collection and small-ticket disbursement rail. Offshore digital EMIs (UK EMD/FCA, Singapore MPI, Hong Kong MSO licence holders) are not treated as banks in mainland China: they cannot hold a PBOC banking licence, cannot access CNAPS or CFETS, and cannot independently complete SAFE trade verification or BOP purpose-code declaration. Their China-reachable services — global collection accounts in USD/EUR, virtual corporate cards, and supplier payment networks — must clear through a licensed PRC partner bank and therefore layer on top of, rather than substitute for, the tier-1 domestic banking relationship. Legal constraints further require that any payment destined for the WFOE ultimately credits a domestic account carrying the entity's Unified Social Credit Code, and any RMB leg must be underwritten by a licensed settlement bank. The WFOE should contractually require the EMI to disclose its onshore settlement-bank agent and maintain a documented fallback to domestic MT103/CNAPS rails in the event of clearing failure or regulatory suspension.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence remains strictly required for a Taiwan-invested WFOE. The legal representative (法定代表人) must appear in person at the selected tier-1 bank's mainland branch for the initial corporate account opening, undergo biometric identification against a Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Residents (台胞证) or passport, and sign the enterprise KYC interview record. Fully remote account opening is not available to foreign-invested enterprises; the PBOC's enterprise account-opening rules mandate an on-site criminal/civil sanctions clearance check of the legal representative and on-site verification of the corporate seal set (公章, 财务章, 法定代表人章). Where the legal representative cannot travel, the bank may accept a written power of attorney notarised in Taiwan and authenticated for mainland use, together with the authorised finance officer's passport and mainland residence permit, but final account activation still requires at least one authorised officer to attend the branch. Select pilot branches of Bank of China and China Merchants Bank (Shanghai, Shenzhen, Xiamen) permit videoconference pre-screening followed by a single on-site visit; none waive the physical meeting component.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity in the cross-strait chain — Taiwan shareholder routed through one or more Hong Kong/Singapore intermediate holding companies, creating a multi-tier attribution problem under PBOC customer due-diligence rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO and control declaration; full-chain corporate registry extracts (Taiwan MOEA business registration, Hong Kong Companies Registry, Singapore ACRA where applicable); register of directors and shareholders for each holding layer; updated articles of association; the WFOE's Business License and Uniform Social Credit Code certificate; board minutes authorising the finance mandate; and audited financial statements of the onshore entity for the most recent two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags in bulk fertiliser wholesale — mismatched cargo values, intermediate-route deviations, and high-frequency same-day payments in the urea/potash line.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Back-to-back chain evidence comprising master supply and purchase contracts, pro-forma and commercial invoices, full-set bills of lading, packing lists, independent weighbridge certificates, SGS/Bureau-Veritas quality certificates, customs declaration records, VAT invoices (增值税发票), and the bank's electronic trade-verification matched report confirming discipline under purpose code 121010 for every outward remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure — urea as a potential dual-use precursor chemical, and potash sourced from Belarus or Russia-listed counterparties triggering OFAC/EU/PBOC denial-list screen hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-of-origin certificates; supplier compliance declarations and end-user certificates; OFAC/EU/PBOC sanctions screening reports for every counterparty and vessel; no-transhipment and no-reflagging warranty clauses in the charter party; UCP/ISBP-compliant LC terms; freight manifest and voyage history; and an independent trade-sanctions advisory opinion in the event any supplier is domiciled in a sanctions-covered jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-injection source-of-funds ambiguity — Taiwan family-office or private-company shareholder remitting large registered-capital tranches without a transparent wealth trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements of the remitting Taiwan entity; Taiwan corporate income-tax filing (营利事业所得税结算申报) and retained-earnings verification; certified audited financial statements of the Taiwan parent; a notarised declaration of lawful source of funds and non-proceeds-of-crime; and a written tax-compliance confirmation for the historical earnings supporting the remittance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) FDI registration — the WFOE's designated tier-1 bank completes the FDI foreign-exchange registration (FDI外汇登记) directly in SAFE's Capital Account Information System, replacing legacy SAFE pre-approval; the registration record references the Foreign Investment Negative List verification and the Unified Social Credit Code. (2) Account structure — open the 资本金账户 (Capital Escrow Account) for receipt of the Taiwan parent's registered capital, together with the corresponding 结汇待支付账户 (RMB Pledge-Settlement Pending Account) for converted RMB awaiting disbursement. (3) Remittance — the Taiwan shareholder instructs its Taiwan or offshore bank to send SWIFT MT103 with the remitter in field 50 exactly matching the SAFE-registered shareholder name, the beneficiary in field 59 citing the WFOE legal name and the capital account number/CNAPS branch identifier, and field 70/72 referencing 'Investment Capital Contribution — [Article] of the Articles of Association'. (4) Verification — the receiving bank validates the remitter against the FDI registration, assigns BOP declaration category '622 — Inbound Direct Investment / Capital Injection', credits the capital account within T+1, and performs capital verification against the registered total investment. (5) Utilization — under the voluntary-settlement regime the WFOE converts to RMB in tranches and disburses only against genuine supporting vouchers: purchase contracts, commercial invoices, payroll and tax records, and operating expense receipts; prohibited uses (securities, wealth management, intercompany on-lending, non-self-use real estate) are hard-blocked by the bank's monitoring logic. (6) Reporting — the WFOE files the annual foreign-investment information report with the market regulator before 30 June each year, and large-sum or pattern-anomalous utilisation triggers SAFE spot-check codes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-side clearing rails: (i) open-account settlements via SWIFT MT103 carrying SAFE purpose code '121010 — General Goods Trade (一般货物贸易)', with each payment matched in the bank's Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System to the electronic customs declaration (报关单) where goods have already cleared customs; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued by the PRC bank as SWIFT MT700/MT720, settled against presentation of full-set clean-on-board bills of lading, commercial invoices, weight certificates, SGS/Bureau-Veritas quality certificates, packing lists, and, where mandated, phytosanitary or fumigation certificates for urea and potash; and (iii) onshore RMB legs cleared through CNAPS (大额支付系统) or the Bulk Interbank Payment System (网上支付跨行清算系统) for domestic bridging, LC discounting, and supplier-finance movements. For bulk agro-chemical charters, the bank will treat any single outbound payment above USD 1,000,000 as an Enhanced Due Diligence transaction requiring the charter-party contract, freight warrant, and a three-month business-trail history before execution. Post-payment documentation must be retained for five years for SAFE verification; an MT103 cannot be released without a valid BOP purpose code, and advance payments exceeding the bank's risk threshold require pre-registration of the underlying trade contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD forwards (远期结售汇) — plain vanilla, executed through the tier-1 settlement bank strictly against documented current-account trade exposure and registered under the real-demand (实需) principle.
Foreign-exchange swaps (外汇掉期) — short-dated liquidity swaps between CNY and USD for working-capital conversion; no speculative open position permitted.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (货币掉期) — for long-term financing liabilities, including SAFE-registered cross-border shareholder loans, with both principal and interest legs fully hedged.

Vanilla CNY/USD options (外汇期权) — calls and puts sold only within an option-spread or collar structure with a documented underlying trade position; naked speculative options are prohibited for onshore entities.

Offshore non-deliverable USD/CNY forwards (NDF) — executed by the Taiwan parent or a group treasury affiliate outside the mainland to offset onshore exposure without triggering direct onshore NDF settlement constraints.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (各地區國稅局)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year WFOE: 1 May to 31 May of the following year; one-month extension to 30 June is available only where the return is accompanied by a certified public accountant (CPA) attestation or is otherwise eligible under the tax-filing extension regime.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: surcharge of 3% of assessed unpaid tax for every two months overdue, up to 9%; statutory interest is additionally assessed. Willful non-filing can trigger tax investigation, back-assessment up to seven years, enforced collection, and, for continued non-operation, administrative dissolution/strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Accounts Filing / Annual Corporate Return (年度決算書表申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Office / online filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end (30 June for a calendar-year company), or within 15 days after shareholder approval if approval is completed later; the filing comprises the business report, balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, and cash-flow statement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA rectification order and administrative fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 for non-filing; repeated failure or evidence of cessation of business for more than six months may support an administrative dissolution/strike-off order under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Resolution / Consent Record and Confirmation of Issued Shareholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained in the statutory minute book; made available to MOEA and the Investment Commission upon inspection or registration request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval of annual financial statements must occur within six months after year-end; a written shareholder resolution is sufficient for a limited-liability WFOE.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain approval within the statutory deadline invalidates the annual accounts filing procedure; non-compliance exposes the company to administrative fines and may render directors personally liable for resulting losses.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory CPA audit is mandatory if paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million or more; if annual revenue reaches NT$100 million or more under the MOEA threshold; or where the MOEA or Investment Commission requires audit in the public interest or as an investment-approval condition. For lower-revenue WFOEs, a CPA-attested tax return is triggered at NT$50 million of annual turnover; otherwise no statutory independent financial-statement audit is required unless the articles or financing arrangements require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in New Taiwan Dollars under the accrual basis pursuant to the Business Entity Accounting Act and Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Standards (EAS; Taiwan GAAP). Public-interest companies and financial institutions apply Taiwan IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. A fertilizer commodity-trader WFOE is treated as a non-public commercial entity under EAS unless it meets the FSC designation thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a separate annual UBO return for an ordinary wholesale WFOE outside designated AML sectors; however, the WFOE must keep an accurate member/shareholder roster and minute book and must annually confirm the roster when the financial statements are approved. Any direct or indirect shareholding transfer by a mainland-China investor requires prior approval from the Investment Commission, and the register must be updated only after MOEA registration of the approved transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (股東會/董事會議事錄)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,200 per year for registered-office and company-secretarial agent services; no mandatory government renewal fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–9,000 per year for a small or medium WFOE, if a CPA audit is required or voluntarily obtained.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (imposed on taxable income exceeding NT$120,000; taxable income not exceeding NT$120,000 is taxed at 0%; AMT applies at 12% on AMT taxable income exceeding the NT$500,000 exemption)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectorial tax holiday for fertilizer wholesaling. Available preferential regimes: (i) 15% tax credit for eligible R&D expenditure (capped at 30% of the current-year tax payable) under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; (ii) 5% surtax only on unappropriated/undistributed earnings; (iii) 10-year loss carryforward, conditional on sound bookkeeping, timely filing and Blue Return or CPA-audited statements; (iv) foreign tax credit for foreign-source income; (v) AMT exemption of NT$500,000 may eliminate AMT exposure for ordinary trading companies.
